adam.name: Adam
adam.role: First man in the Genesis account
adam.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
adam.importance: God puts him in the garden of Eden to work and keep it. God tells him not to eat from one tree. He eats the fruit that Eve gives him. God sends him out to farm the ground.
adam.connections: Husband of Eve. Father of Cain, Abel, and Seth.

eve.name: Eve
eve.role: First woman in the Genesis account
eve.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
eve.importance: The serpent talks with her, and she eats the fruit. She gives some to Adam. Adam names her Eve, the mother of all the living. She later names Seth as the child God gave in place of Abel.
eve.connections: Wife of Adam. Mother of Cain, Abel, and Seth.

cain.name: Cain
cain.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
cain.importance: He farms the ground and brings an offering. God respects Abel’s offering and not his. He kills Abel in the field. God sends him away, and he lives in the land of Nod.
cain.connections: Son of Adam and Eve. Brother of Abel. Father of the Enoch in Cain’s line.

abel.name: Abel
abel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abel.importance: He keeps sheep and brings an offering from his flock. God respects him and his offering. Cain kills him in the field. God says Abel’s blood cries from the ground.
abel.connections: Son of Adam and Eve. Brother of Cain.

enoch.name: Enoch
enoch.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
enoch.importance: He walks with God for three hundred years after Methuselah’s birth. Then he is not found, for God takes him. Moses 6–7 gives him a larger part in LDS scripture.
enoch.connections: Son of Jared in Seth’s line. Father of Methuselah. Cain’s son Enoch is another man.

noah.name: Noah
noah.role: Builder of the ship in the flood
noah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
noah.importance: God tells him to build a ship, and he does all that God commands. He takes his family and the animals inside. After the flood he builds an altar. God makes a covenant never to destroy the earth by flood again.
noah.connections: Son of Lamech. Father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

shem.name: Shem
shem.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shem.importance: He and Japheth cover their father Noah without looking at him. Noah blesses the LORD, the God of Shem. Genesis 11 follows his line down to Terah and Abram.
shem.connections: Brother of Ham and Japheth. Abram comes from his line.

ham.name: Ham
ham.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ham.importance: He sees his father Noah uncovered and tells his two brothers. Noah then curses Ham’s son Canaan, not Ham. The passage gives no support for racial slavery.
ham.connections: Father of Canaan. Brother of Shem and Japheth.

japheth.name: Japheth
japheth.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
japheth.importance: He helps Shem cover their father Noah. Noah asks God to enlarge Japheth. Genesis 10 lists his sons and the peoples that come from them.

nimrod.name: Nimrod
nimrod.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nimrod.importance: He becomes a mighty one on the earth. People say, “like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD.” His kingdom begins with Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in Shinar.
nimrod.connections: Son of Cush. Grandson of Ham.

abraham.name: Abraham
abraham.role: Man God calls to Canaan and promises a nation
abraham.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abraham.importance: God tells him to leave Haran, and he goes to Canaan. Out of fear he twice calls Sarah his sister. God promises him land and a son, and Sarah bears Isaac. He goes to offer Isaac, and the LORD’s angel stops him.
abraham.connections: Husband of Sarah. Father of Ishmael and Isaac. Uncle of Lot.

sarah.name: Sarah
sarah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
sarah.importance: She has no child and gives Hagar to Abram. She then treats Hagar harshly. She laughs when she hears she will bear a son. She bears Isaac and tells Abraham to send Hagar and Ishmael away.
sarah.connections: Wife of Abraham. Mistress of Hagar.

lot.name: Lot
lot.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
lot.importance: He parts from Abram and chooses the plain of the Jordan near Sodom. Kings carry him off, and Abram rescues him. Two angels lead him out before Sodom is destroyed. His two daughters later make him drunk and bear his sons.
lot.connections: Son of Haran. Father of two daughters in Genesis 19.

hagar.name: Hagar
hagar.role: Egyptian servant and mother of Ishmael
hagar.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hagar.importance: She conceives by Abram and runs from Sarai’s harsh treatment. The LORD’s angel finds her by a spring. She calls the LORD “a God who sees.” Later Abraham sends her away, and God hears her son’s voice.
hagar.connections: Servant of Sarah. Mother of Ishmael, Abraham’s first son.

ishmael.name: Ishmael
ishmael.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ishmael.importance: The LORD’s angel tells Hagar to name him Ishmael. Abraham sends him away with Hagar, and God hears his voice. God promises to make him a great nation. He and Isaac later bury Abraham.
ishmael.connections: Half-brother of Isaac. Father of twelve princes.

melchizedek.name: Melchizedek
melchizedek.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
melchizedek.importance: He brings out bread and wine after Abram rescues Lot. He blesses Abram and blesses God Most High. Abram gives him a tenth of all. LDS scripture says more about his work as priest.
melchizedek.connections: Genesis names no family for him. He meets Abram after Lot’s rescue.

isaac.name: Isaac
isaac.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
isaac.importance: God promises him to Abraham and Sarah, and Sarah bears him. Abraham binds him on an altar, and God provides a ram. He marries Rebekah and digs his father’s wells again. When he is old and cannot see, he blesses Jacob in place of Esau.
isaac.connections: Husband of Rebekah. Father of Esau and Jacob.

rebekah.name: Rebekah
rebekah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
rebekah.importance: She draws water for Abraham’s servant and his camels. She agrees to go to Canaan and marry Isaac. She bears twins, Esau and Jacob, and loves Jacob. She dresses Jacob as Esau so that Isaac blesses him.
rebekah.connections: Daughter of Bethuel. Sister of Laban. Wife of Isaac.

abimelech.name: Abimelech
abimelech.role: King who deals with Abraham and Isaac
abimelech.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abimelech.importance: He takes Sarah, and God warns him in a dream. He gives her back and swears an oath with Abraham at Beersheba. In Genesis 26 an Abimelech learns that Rebekah is Isaac’s wife. Genesis does not say if this is the same king.
abimelech.connections: He deals with Abraham in Genesis 20–21. An Abimelech deals with Isaac in Genesis 26. Phicol leads his army.

esau.name: Esau
esau.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
esau.importance: He sells his birthright to Jacob for bread and lentil stew. Jacob then takes his blessing, and Esau plans to kill him. Years later he runs to meet Jacob and kisses him. He settles in the hill country of Seir.
esau.connections: Twin brother of Jacob. Ancestor of Edom.

jacob.name: Jacob
jacob.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jacob.importance: He buys Esau’s birthright and tricks Isaac to get the blessing. Laban then tricks him, and he works twenty years for Laban. He wrestles a man at night and is named Israel. In old age he goes to Egypt to see Joseph.
jacob.connections: Son of Isaac and Rebekah. Father of twelve sons and Dinah.

laban.name: Laban
laban.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
laban.importance: He welcomes Abraham’s servant and lets Rebekah go. He gives Jacob Leah in place of Rachel after seven years of work. Jacob says Laban changed his wages ten times. Laban chases Jacob to Gilead, and they make a covenant there.
laban.connections: Father of Leah and Rachel. Jacob works for him.

leah.name: Leah
leah.role: Mother of six sons and Dinah
leah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
leah.importance: Laban gives her to Jacob in place of Rachel. Jacob loves Rachel more, and the LORD gives Leah children. She names Reuben for her pain and Judah for her praise. Jacob buries her in the cave of Machpelah.
leah.connections: Daughter of Laban. Wife of Jacob. Sister of Rachel.

rachel.name: Rachel
rachel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
rachel.importance: Jacob loves her and works fourteen years for her and Leah. She has no child for years, then bears Joseph. She takes her father’s teraphim when the family leaves. She dies giving birth to Benjamin on the way to Ephrath.
rachel.connections: Daughter of Laban. Wife of Jacob. Sister of Leah.

bilhah.name: Bilhah
bilhah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
bilhah.importance: Laban gives her to Rachel as a servant. Rachel gives her to Jacob, and she bears Dan and Naphtali. Rachel names both boys. Reuben later lies with her, and Genesis gives her no words.
bilhah.connections: Rachel’s servant. Mother of two of Jacob’s sons.

zilpah.name: Zilpah
zilpah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zilpah.importance: Laban gives her to Leah as a servant. Leah gives her to Jacob, and she bears Gad and Asher. Leah names both boys. Genesis gives Zilpah no words.
zilpah.connections: Leah’s servant. Mother of two of Jacob’s sons.

dinah.name: Dinah
dinah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
dinah.importance: She goes out to see the daughters of the land. Shechem, son of Hamor, takes her and lies with her. Simeon and Levi kill the city’s men and take her from Shechem’s house. Genesis gives her no words.

joseph.name: Joseph
joseph.role: Son sold into Egypt who later rules under Pharaoh
joseph.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
joseph.importance: His brothers hate him and sell him, and he is taken to Egypt. Potiphar’s wife accuses him falsely, and he goes to prison. He explains Pharaoh’s dreams and stores grain for the famine. He feeds his family and tells his brothers God meant it for good.
joseph.connections: Son of Jacob and Rachel. Husband of Asenath. Father of Ephraim and Manasseh.

judah.name: Judah
judah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
judah.importance: He tells his brothers to sell Joseph and not kill him. He keeps Tamar from his son Shelah, then says she is more righteous. He promises Jacob to bring Benjamin back. In Egypt he offers to stay as a slave in Benjamin’s place.
judah.connections: Son of Jacob and Leah. Father of Perez and Zerah through Tamar.

reuben.name: Reuben
reuben.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
reuben.importance: He lies with Bilhah, and his father hears of it. He tells his brothers not to kill Joseph and plans to bring him home. He offers his two sons as a pledge for Benjamin. Jacob says Reuben will not excel.
reuben.connections: Son of Jacob and Leah. Brother of Joseph.

simeon.name: Simeon
simeon.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
simeon.importance: He and Levi kill the men of Shechem after Shechem defiles Dinah. Joseph later binds him and keeps him in Egypt. He goes free when the brothers bring Benjamin. Jacob curses the anger of Simeon and Levi.

levi.name: Levi
levi.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
levi.importance: He and Simeon kill the men of Shechem and take Dinah away. Jacob says they have brought him trouble. In his last words Jacob curses their anger and says he will scatter them.

benjamin.name: Benjamin
benjamin.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
benjamin.importance: Rachel dies at his birth and names him Benoni, but Jacob names him Benjamin. Jacob fears to send him to Egypt. Joseph’s cup is found in his sack. Judah offers to stay as a slave in his place.
benjamin.connections: Son of Jacob and Rachel. Full brother of Joseph.

tamar.name: Tamar
tamar.role: Judah’s daughter-in-law who bears his twin sons
tamar.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
tamar.importance: Judah sends her home and does not give her to his son Shelah. She veils herself, and Judah lies with her without knowing her. She keeps his signet, cords, and staff. When Judah sees them he says she is more righteous.
tamar.connections: Widow of Er and Onan. Mother of Perez and Zerah.

potiphar.name: Potiphar
potiphar.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
potiphar.importance: He buys Joseph and puts him over his whole house. His wife says Joseph tried to lie with her. He grows angry and puts Joseph in the king’s prison.
potiphar.connections: Husband of the unnamed woman who accuses Joseph.

pharaoh.name: Pharaoh
pharaoh.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
pharaoh.importance: In Genesis 12 a Pharaoh takes Sarai and then sends Abram away. In Joseph’s time a Pharaoh dreams of seven fat and seven thin cattle. He sets Joseph over Egypt and gives Jacob’s family land in Goshen. Genesis names no Pharaoh.
pharaoh.connections: The Pharaoh of Genesis 12 deals with Abram and Sarai. A later Pharaoh deals with Joseph and Jacob.

asenath.name: Asenath
asenath.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
asenath.importance: Pharaoh gives her to Joseph as a wife. She bears Manasseh and Ephraim before the famine. Genesis tells nothing else about her.
asenath.connections: Daughter of Potiphera, priest of On. Mother of Manasseh and Ephraim.

ephraim.name: Ephraim
ephraim.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ephraim.importance: He is born in Egypt before the famine. Jacob takes him as his own son. Jacob puts his right hand on Ephraim, the younger. Jacob says the younger brother will be greater.
ephraim.connections: Son of Joseph and Asenath. Brother of Manasseh.

manasseh.name: Manasseh
manasseh.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
manasseh.importance: He is Joseph’s firstborn, born in Egypt. Jacob takes him as his own son. Jacob puts his left hand on Manasseh and his right on Ephraim. Joseph objects, but Jacob says Manasseh will also be great.
manasseh.connections: Son of Joseph and Asenath. Brother of Ephraim.
